title: Yuan, Ming and Qing Literature
full_title: Literature of the Yuan, Ming and Qing Dynasties
tagline: Yuan drama, *The Western Chamber*, *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, *Water Margin*, *Journey to the West*, *The Plum in the Golden Vase* and the vernacular story, Ming and Qing drama, *Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio*, *The Scholars*, *Dream of the Red Chamber*, and Ming and Qing poetry, prose and criticism
summary: From the Yuan to the Qing, drama and the vernacular novel became the great literary forms, while classical poetry and prose went on flourishing. This course reads Yuan drama from Guan Hanqing to *The Western Chamber*; the Ming novels *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, *Water Margin*, *Journey to the West* and *The Plum in the Golden Vase*; Tang Xianzu’s *Peony Pavilion*; Pu Songling’s tales; *The Scholars* and *Dream of the Red Chamber*; and the poetry, prose and criticism of the late empire.
overview: The literature of the later dynasties (1271–1911): drama and the long vernacular novel take the centre, while poetry and prose retreat into schools, anthologies and scholarship.

The course treats the four great novels as four different solutions to one problem—how to build a large narrative without a lyric centre—and treats drama as the age's true collaborative art: playwright, troupe, theatre, censor.
It closes with Ming-Qing criticism: how fanbi, commentary and textual scholarship became the period's most adventurous form of writing.
outcomes: Explain the institution of the zaju troupe (four acts and a wedge, one singer, role types) and its effect on plot
Place The Orphan of Zhao and The Romance of the Western Chamber in the moral history of drama
Compare the Ming novels as genre solutions: history, rebellion, cultivation
Explain what The Plum in the Golden Vase adds: household economics and the retirement of the hero
Read Qing drama—The Peony Pavilion, The Peach-Blossom Fan, The Palace of Eternal Life—as three attitudes to feeling and dynastic fall
Analyise Strange Tales' use of the classical tale to discuss examinations, justice and the marvellous
Explain The Scholars' episodic satire and its economics of reputation
Assess Dream of the Red Chamber's revisions, commentary traditions and the two ending systems
Trace Ming-Qing poetic schools and Tongcheng prose as programmes, and fanbi criticism as a literary form

chapters.title: Yuan drama
chapters.summary: The form of *zaju* — four acts and a wedge, with one lead singer — and Guan Hanqing’s *Injustice to Dou E*.

chapters.title: *The Western Chamber* and other playwrights
chapters.summary: Wang Shifu’s *The Western Chamber*, Bai Pu and Ma Zhiyuan, and Yuan *sanqu* songs.

chapters.title: *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*
chapters.summary: History and fiction, how the novel was made, and its characters and battles.

chapters.title: *Water Margin*
chapters.summary: The outlaws of Liangshan, the versions of the novel, and its heroes and its violence.

chapters.title: *Journey to the West*
chapters.summary: Xuanzang’s pilgrimage turned into comic fantasy, Sun Wukong, and readings of the novel.

chapters.title: *The Plum in the Golden Vase* and the vernacular story
chapters.summary: The first Chinese novel of domestic life, its realism and its reputation, and the story collections of Feng Menglong and Ling Mengchu.

chapters.title: Ming and Qing drama
chapters.summary: Tang Xianzu’s *The Peony Pavilion*, Kunqu opera, Hong Sheng’s *The Palace of Eternal Youth* and Kong Shangren’s *The Peach Blossom Fan*.

chapters.title: *Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio*
chapters.summary: Pu Songling’s tales of fox spirits and ghosts written in classical Chinese, and the classical tale after him.

chapters.title: *The Scholars*
chapters.summary: Wu Jingzi’s satire of the examination system and the literati it produced.

chapters.title: *Dream of the Red Chamber*
chapters.summary: Cao Xueqin’s novel, the problem of its last forty chapters, its world and characters, and two centuries of Redology.

chapters.title: Ming and Qing poetry, prose and criticism
chapters.summary: Schools of poetry and prose from the Former Seven Masters to the Tongcheng school, Yuan Mei, and the criticism of Jin Shengtan and Wang Fuzhi.

history.title: The troupe economy
history.detail: Homeless scholars and commercial troupes meet in Dadu and Hangzhou: zaju's golden decade.

history.title: A drama of loyalty
history.detail: The Orphan of Zhao circulates in print; a few years later the Ming house begins.

history.title: The novel printed
history.detail: Jiajing editions of the Three Kingdoms and Water Margin spread; the marketplace discovers that length can be sold.

history.title: The monkey on the shelf
history.detail: The Jinling printing of Journey to the West appears; allegory becomes a reading policy.

history.title: The household novel
history.detail: A printed Jin Ping Mei circulates with a preface praising it as advice about desire; the everyday becomes a subject.

history.title: Feeling on trial
history.detail: The Peach-Blossom Fan and the Palace of Eternal Life bring feeling and dynastic fall to the Kangxi stage; both authors soon leave office.

history.title: The scholars satirised
history.detail: The Scholars circulates; examination culture is interviewed by a novelist.

history.title: The stone's story complete
history.detail: The Cheng printing fixes a hundred and twenty chapters; commentary and sequel wars continue.
history.people: Cao Xueqin, Gao E, Zhang Zhupo
